the lateral force exerted by a ball or bar attachments on a 20 inclined mini implant is higher than that on a vertical mini implant and that the lateral force on a mini implant with a bar attachment is less than that on a mini implant ball attachment.
the bar attachment was better than the ball attachment in reducing lateral forces on the inclined implant.
mini implants are subjected more stress when tilted and that a bar attachment is more effective at reducing lateral stress than a ball attachment when a mini implant is tilted.
In summary, our research is concerned with
a new approach to the problem of lateral forces exerted through bar attachments in relation the inclination of mini implants.
the lateral forces exerted to the mini implant in the overdenture with ball or bar attachment in the inclined position.
the influence of lateral forces exerted through bar or ball attachments in relation to mini implant inclination.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the lateral force borne by mini implants is affected by the inclination of the mini implant and type of attachment.
a bar attachment can help reduce the stress on the mini implants when one mini implant is inclined at 20 degrees.
a CAD/CAM fabricated titanium bar attachment may be more suitable than the ball attachments when mini implants are tilted.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

a mini implant with a ball attachment should be used when the mini implant is inclined at less than 10deg and a mini implant with bar attachment should be used for a mini implant inclined more than 10deg.

the bar attachment was superior to the ball attachment in reducing the lateral forces exerted by the inclined mini implants, and this effect was more prominent when one mini implant was inclined at 20 deg.
the mini implants should be inserted vertically to minimize lateral force and bar attachments should be used to reduce the lateral forces on mini implants.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the lateral forces borne on mini implants are affected by the inclination and type of attachment.
mini implants with ball attachment are more susceptible to lateral forces, especially when the mini implant is tilted.
the bar attachment can reduce lateral force borne by mini implant when one of them is inclined at 20 degrees.
